Class 5: Area, perimeter and angles

Read original figures, distinguish their properties and use the conditions shown in a diagram.

ExploreArea and composite shapes

A step-shaped plot is built from a 7 by 5 unit rectangle with a 1 by 2 unit corner removed, as shown. What is its area in square units?

  1. A2
  2. B33
  3. C35
  4. D18

Choose an answer.

Need a hint?

Find the area of the whole rectangle, then subtract the area of the missing corner.

Answer & method
Answer B: 33

The whole rectangle is 7 x 5 = 35 square units; the missing corner is 1 x 2 = 2, so the shape covers 35 - 2 = 33 square units.

ReasonArea and composite shapes

A rectangular plot is 3 times as long as it is wide. Its perimeter is 80 m. What is its area?

  1. A390 sq m
  2. B300 sq m
  3. C330 sq m
  4. D800 sq m

Choose an answer.

Need a hint?

Half the perimeter is length plus width. Split it using the ratio of length to width.

Answer & method
Answer B: 300 sq m

Length + width = 40 m, made of 4 equal parts. Width = 10 m, length = 30 m. Area = 300 sq m.

Try more in game →

StretchAngles

Three angles sit on a straight line. Two of them measure 44° and 26°. What is the third angle?

  1. A110°
  2. B136°
  3. C70°
  4. D130°

Choose an answer.

Need a hint?

Angles on a straight line always add up to 180 degrees, even when there are three of them.

Answer & method
Answer A: 110°

180° - 44° - 26° = 110°.

For grown-ups

Ideas to practise

  • Area and composite shapes. Find the area of the whole and subtract missing parts. Boundary lengths and square units answer different questions.
  • Perimeter. Add the lengths around the outside. Do not confuse perimeter with area.
  • Angles. A right angle is 90 degrees; a straight angle is 180 degrees.
  • Solids and nets. Follow which faces meet when folded. A face touching another in the net cannot be opposite it.
  • Measurement and conversions. Use the same unit before adding or comparing measurements.
  • Reflection and symmetry. A mirror reverses left and right, but not top and bottom.
  • Shapes and their properties. Count straight sides and corners carefully. A curved edge is not a straight side.

Using the feedback

Learning reports distinguish hinted answers from independent first choices. They consider up to 20 recent different, unhinted questions per skill and level, and wait for at least five before suggesting extra practice. Repeating the same question does not add evidence. Reports are practice evidence, not IQ scores, diagnoses, ranks or predictions of competition results.

Ask the learner to explain a drawing or check with objects too. Choose Explore or an earlier chapter when a step feels too large.
